In May 2022 the CFPB ordered **Bank of America, N.A.** to pay a **USD 10 million** civil money penalty and refund or cancel at least USD 592,000 in fees over how it processed **garnishment notices**, the court orders that let creditors take funds from a debtor's account.

The CFPB found **unfair and deceptive** practices: the deposit agreement made customers waive the bank's liability for garnishment protections and told them they could not go to court to stop wrongful garnishments. The bank also froze accounts and sent funds where state law did not allow it, and sometimes applied the wrong state's exemption rules.

**Lesson:** debt-related processes inside the bank, not just collection calls, carry consumer protection risk. Contract wording and back-office procedures need compliance review and trained staff.

Source: CFPB enforcement action page, docket 2022-CFPB-0002.

cards.title: Prepare for the consumer compliance exam
cards.prompt: Put Maya's final-week steps in a sensible order.
steps: Confirm the board and management have received current compliance and complaint reports
Check policies and procedures cover every product, including the new rewards account
Pull training schedules, materials and completion records by role, including vendors
Review monitoring and audit results and show what was fixed
Summarise complaint trends, escalations, root causes and remediation
Brief staff who will meet examiners on facts, not guesses

cards.back: Companies generally respond within 15 days; if more time is needed, they say so and give a final response within 60 days.
For notices sent by mail, 30 days to opt out is given as a reasonable opportunity.
Collects debts owed to another, or a creditor collecting its own debts under a name suggesting a third party.
Strong, satisfactory, deficient, seriously deficient or critically deficient.
Periodic, covering federal and state law for each originator's work: 1026.36(f)(3)(iii).
10 business days, or 45 days (90 in set cases) with provisional credit.

cards.question: Tom's team plans to start sharing customer data with an unaffiliated insurer for marketing. No Regulation P exception applies. What must happen before sharing?
options: Nothing, if the insurer signs a confidentiality agreement
Only a note in the next annual report
Notice, an opt-out notice and a reasonable opportunity to opt out, and no opt-out received
Approval from the CFPB
cards.explanation: Under 12 CFR 1016.10, the bank may not share nonpublic personal information with a nonaffiliated third party outside the exceptions unless it has given the initial and opt-out notices, a reasonable chance to opt out, and the consumer has not opted out.

cards.title: Stage five take-aways
items: Record complaints from every channel, escalate legal and harm issues, fix root causes and remediate.
On the CFPB portal, companies generally respond within 15 days, and give a final response within 60 when more time is needed.
Regulation P requires initial and generally annual privacy notices and an opt-out before most sharing with nonaffiliated third parties.
Regulation F reaches third-party collectors and creditors that collect under another name; bank collections still carry UDAAP risk.
Exam readiness means evidence: reports, policies, training records, monitoring, audit and complaint analysis.

cards.prompt: You have finished the five stages. Which one part of your bank's compliance management system would you strengthen first in your own role, and what evidence would show an examiner it works?

quiz.question: According to the CFPB's complaint process page, how quickly do companies generally respond to complaints sent through the CFPB?
options: Within 2 days
Within 15 days
Within 90 days
Within one year
quiz.explanation: The CFPB says companies generally respond in 15 days; in some cases they say the response is in progress and give a final response within 60 days.

quiz.question: Which complaint would the CFPB manual expect to be escalated, not just resolved?
options: One about a long wait on the phone line
One praising a branch employee by name
One asking for a replacement debit card to be posted urgently overseas
One alleging an account was opened without the customer's consent
quiz.explanation: The manual lists complaints raising issues such as unauthorised account openings, discrimination or improper sales as ones that must be categorised and escalated.

quiz.question: When must a bank give its initial privacy notice to a new customer under Regulation P?
options: Within one year of opening the account
Only when the customer asks to see it
After the customer receives the first annual account statement
No later than when the customer relationship is established
quiz.explanation: 12 CFR 1016.4(a)(1) requires the initial notice no later than when the bank establishes a customer relationship, subject to limited exceptions.

quiz.question: When can a bank skip the annual privacy notice under Regulation P?
options: When the customer uses the bank's mobile app instead of paper
When it shares only under the exceptions and its practices are unchanged
When the customer holds fewer than three accounts with the bank
Whenever the bank also posts its full privacy notice on its public website
quiz.explanation: 1016.5(e) excuses the annual notice if the bank discloses information only under 1016.13-1016.15 and has not changed its policies and practices since the last notice.

quiz.question: The bank mails privacy and opt-out notices. Which opt-out window does Regulation P give as an example of a reasonable opportunity?
options: 3 days
10 days
30 days
180 days
quiz.explanation: 1016.10(a)(3)(i) gives 30 days from mailing as an example of a reasonable opportunity to opt out by mail.

quiz.question: Under Regulation F, when can a bank collecting its own debts be treated as a debt collector?
options: When it uses a name suggesting a third party is collecting
Whenever it collects any overdue debt of its own
Only when the debt is larger than USD 10,000
Never, because banks are always fully exempt from Regulation F
quiz.explanation: 12 CFR 1006.2(i) includes a creditor that, collecting its own debts, uses any name other than its own that would suggest a third party is collecting.

quiz.question: Complaints show many customers are surprised by the same overdraft fee. Which response best fits CMS expectations?
options: Close each complaint with a standard apology letter
Find the root cause, fix the practice and consider remediation
Remove the fee from the complaint category list
Wait for a regulator to raise the issue at the next examination
quiz.explanation: The manual expects management to monitor complaints for harm and CMS weaknesses and take prospective and retrospective corrective action.

quiz.question: In the 2022 Bank of America garnishment case, which practice did the CFPB find?
options: Refusing to process any garnishment orders at all
Charging no fees at all for processing garnishments
Paying garnished funds over to judgment creditors too slowly, causing them losses
Telling consumers they could not go to court to stop wrongful garnishments
quiz.explanation: The CFPB found the bank misrepresented that consumers could not go to court to prevent wrongful garnishments and required waivers of liability in its deposit agreement.

quiz.question: Which of these is NOT something examiners assess about complaint handling under the CFPB manual?
options: Whether every complaint was resolved in the customer's favour
Whether complaints from all channels are recorded
Whether investigations and responses are reasonable
Whether complaints lead to appropriate corrective action by management
quiz.explanation: Examiners assess processes, reasonableness, recording, timeliness, escalation and corrective action. A good-faith effort is expected, not a guaranteed customer win.

quiz.question: An examiner asks how training changed after last year's complaint trends. What is the best evidence?
options: A statement that staff were reminded about it verbally
The original training materials from three years ago
Updated training on the complaint issues, with completion records
A list of staff who complained about the length of the training itself
quiz.explanation: Examiners request training developed in response to issues raised in complaints, plus records showing who completed it.

regulators: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC)
Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System

references.title: CFPB Supervision and Examination Manual: Compliance Management Review
references.note: Training is a reviewed component of the compliance management system; examiners check content, completion and updates. Also sets complaint response expectations.

references.title: Comptroller's Handbook: Compliance Management Systems
references.note: OCC examiner expectations for the consumer compliance management system, including training.

references.title: CFPB Examination Procedures: Unfair, Deceptive, or Abusive Acts or Practices
references.note: Sets out the unfairness, deception and abuse standards and the role of complaints; examiners review training materials and incentive plans.

references.title: 12 CFR Part 1005 Electronic Fund Transfers (Regulation E)

references.title: 12 CFR 1026.36 Prohibited acts or practices and certain requirements for credit secured by a dwelling

references.title: 12 CFR 1026.19 Certain mortgage and variable-rate transactions
references.note: Timing of the Loan Estimate and Closing Disclosure and the limit on fees before the Loan Estimate is received.

references.title: Equal Credit Opportunity Act (ECOA) examination procedures

references.note: Initial and annual privacy notices, the annual notice exception, and the opt-out before sharing with nonaffiliated third parties.

references.title: 12 CFR 1006.2 Definitions (Regulation F)
references.note: Defines debt collector, including a creditor collecting its own debts under a name suggesting a third party.

references.title: Learn how the complaint process works
references.note: Companies generally respond to complaints sent through the CFPB within 15 days, with a final response within 60 days where more time is needed.

bank.question: Prairie Lantern Bank, a national bank with USD 14 billion in assets, is preparing for a consumer compliance exam. Which statement about its supervisors is most accurate?
options: Only the OCC can examine it, because it is a national bank
The CFPB examines it for federal consumer financial law, and the OCC remains its prudential supervisor
Only the FDIC examines it, because its deposits are insured
FinCEN examines it for consumer law under the Bank Secrecy Act
bank.explanation: Above USD 10 billion in assets, the CFPB supervises a bank for federal consumer financial law. The OCC still charters and supervises the national bank prudentially. FinCEN is about the BSA, not consumer law.

bank.question: A bank's compliance policies are excellent, but staff in a new digital lending team have never been trained on them. How would an examiner most likely see this?
options: As acceptable, because the written policies are what examiners rate
As a problem only once customers have already started to complain about it
As a matter for the HR department, which sits outside the CMS
As a CMS weakness, since training must reinforce policy for each role
bank.explanation: Training is one of the four parts of the compliance programme. Policies that staff do not know do not protect consumers, and examiners check that training is tailored and consistent with policy.

bank.question: The board of a bank receives no reports on consumer complaints or compliance issues. Which CMS component is weakest?
options: Monitoring and/or audit
Consumer complaint response
Policies and procedures manual
Board and management oversight
bank.explanation: Board and management oversight includes receiving relevant compliance information and acting on it. Without reports, the board cannot carry out its oversight role, even if other parts exist.

bank.question: A bank outsources its collections calls to a vendor. The vendor's agents use a script the bank never reviewed, and complaints rise. Which response best fits the CFPB's expectations?
options: Tell complainants to take their concerns to the vendor directly
Review and approve the script, require vendor training and monitor calls
End the contract at once and stop collecting overdue debts
Note in the file that the vendor carries all of the responsibility by contract
bank.explanation: The bank cannot outsource responsibility for compliance. It should oversee the provider's procedures, training and conduct, including scripts, and monitor results.

bank.question: Which approach to compliance training is most consistent with what CFPB examiners look for?
options: One annual course for all staff, unchanged unless the law changes
Training only for the compliance department, who then answer any staff questions
Role-based modules updated before rule and product changes, with completion tracking
Optional e-learning that staff can take when they have time
bank.explanation: The manual expects training to be comprehensive, timely, tailored to responsibilities, updated in advance of changes, and tracked, with follow-up for late completers.

bank.question: An audit finds that branch staff misdescribe a savings account's fee waiver. Management commits to a fix. What should examiners later be able to see?
options: Training built in response to the finding, and evidence staff completed it
A note that the account has since been renamed
A statement from staff that they will be more careful
Nothing, because audit findings are kept confidential
bank.explanation: Examiners request training developed as a result of management's commitments to address audit, monitoring or exam findings and complaint issues. They expect to see the content and completion.

bank.question: In the 2023 Bank of America order on credit card rewards, what did the CFPB find about a sign-up bonus?
options: It was so generous that it raised safety and soundness concerns
It was shown as open to all but refused to applicants in some channels
It was paid to the bank's employees instead of to the customers
It was found lawful because the conditions were set out in the fine print
bank.explanation: The CFPB found deception: the bonus was advertised online in a way that made it seem open to all applicants, but those applying by phone or in branch were denied it. Some promised bonuses were not paid due to employee error.

bank.question: A bank's sales incentive plan pays staff per new account. Which control set best reflects the CFPB manual's expectations?
options: Higher incentives for staff who open the most products each month
Deleting older consent records to save storage and reduce cost
Letting each branch design its own incentive rules and targets
Compensation review, training on consent and accurate terms, and a speak-up route
bank.explanation: The manual asks examiners to review incentive structures and training on ethics, reporting, accurate descriptions and consent evidence. These are the controls that would have prevented harms like the Wells Fargo case.

bank.question: An examiner concludes that a bank's training programme has significant gaps that are likely to lead to violations. Which rating language would match the CFPB scale?
options: Deficient or seriously deficient
Amber or red status
Pass or fail outcome
Level 1 or Level 2 rating
bank.explanation: The CFPB manual asks examiners to conclude whether each element is strong, satisfactory, deficient, seriously deficient or critically deficient.

bank.question: A bank launches a 'zero-fee' overdraft line. A fee applies after the first 30 days, disclosed on page 9 of the agreement. Staff are told not to mention it unless asked. What is the strongest UDAAP concern?
options: Unfairness, because every kind of overdraft fee is illegal under federal law
Deception: the headline's net impression misleads and fine print may not cure it
No concern at all, because the fee is written into the account agreement
Abusiveness, because any fee charged on a line of credit always counts as abusive
bank.explanation: The net impression of 'zero-fee' is misleading, the fee is material and staff are told to stay silent. Fine print may not cure a misleading headline.

bank.question: Which fact pattern best fits the 'not reasonably avoidable' element of unfairness?
options: A fee the customer chose to pay after a clear and full explanation
A fee that is waived when customers sign up for low-balance alerts
A fee triggered by a merchant's re-presentment the customer can't control
A fee shown clearly on screen before each transaction is confirmed by the customer
bank.explanation: Consumers cannot reasonably avoid harm they cannot control or foresee. Re-presentment timing is set by the merchant, as in the repeat NSF fee case.

bank.question: An older customer relies on a banker who says a product is 'right for you', and the banker sells a costly add-on the customer clearly doesn't understand. Which UDAAP limb fits best?
options: Abusive: unreasonable advantage of reliance and lack of understanding
Unfair: the add-on product was not profitable for the bank
Deceptive: the product's official name was far too long
None: the customer signed all the paperwork, so the sale is lawful
bank.explanation: The abusive standard covers taking unreasonable advantage of a consumer's lack of understanding or reasonable reliance on the provider to act in their interest.

bank.question: A marketing manager argues: 'We didn't intend to mislead, so it can't be deceptive.' What is the correct response?
options: Correct: intent to mislead is the key element of deception
Intent is not needed; the test is whether a reasonable consumer is misled
Correct, unless the regulator can prove bad faith by the bank
Intent matters only for unfairness, so deception is ruled out
bank.explanation: Deception does not require intent. The test is whether the practice is likely to mislead a reasonable consumer and is material.

bank.question: Under the CFPB's UDAAP procedures, which documents would examiners typically request early to spot UDAAP risk?
options: Only the audited financial statements and auditor's letter
Only board meeting minutes on capital and dividend policy
Only IT system architecture diagrams and data centre network maps
Training materials, pay plans, disclosures and complaint records
bank.explanation: The document review step lists items such as training materials, product lists and disclosures, procedure manuals, minutes, monitoring and audit materials, compensation arrangements and complaints.

bank.question: The 2022 Wells Fargo order covered deposit accounts. Which deposit practice did the CFPB find unfair?
options: Freezing accounts on suspected fraud when lesser restraints were available
Paying interest above the advertised savings rate
Offering more branch locations than competitors
Sending monthly account statements by email only
bank.explanation: The CFPB found Wells Fargo unfairly froze consumer accounts in suspected fraud cases when lesser restraints were available, alongside deceptive claims on fee waivers and unfair overdraft fees.

bank.question: Which statement about puffery is consistent with the CFPB procedures?
options: Any marketing adjective at all is deceptive
Puffery is deceptive once any customer complains
Exaggeration no reasonable consumer would take seriously is not deceptive
Puffery is allowed only in television adverts
bank.explanation: The procedures say exaggerated claims or puffery are not deceptive if a reasonable consumer would not take them seriously.

bank.question: A bank sees 200 complaints in a month saying customers didn't understand a new card's interest rate structure. What does the CFPB guidance suggest examiners do with this?
options: Ignore it unless a court finds a violation
Count it only if each complaint is in writing
Treat it as a red flag and review the practice in detail
Assume it reflects customer error and move on
bank.explanation: The UDAAP procedures say complaints alleging consumers did not understand terms may be a red flag warranting a detailed review, especially when many similar complaints concern the same product.

bank.question: A UDAAP review weighs costs and benefits under the unfairness test. Which is an offsetting benefit the test can consider?
options: Lower prices or wider product availability for consumers
Higher fee income for the bank
Lower staff training costs overall
A higher share price for investors
bank.explanation: Countervailing benefits are to consumers or competition, such as lower prices or wider availability. The costs of preventing the injury are also considered, but bank profit alone is not a consumer benefit.

bank.question: A customer phones on Monday to dispute an online transfer. The bank requires written confirmation. The letter arrives 14 business days later. The bank has not yet decided. Which statement is correct?
options: The bank may close the case because the written letter arrived late
The bank must keep investigating but did not have to give provisional credit
The bank must pay interest on the disputed amount at double the rate
The bank must restart the 10-business-day clock from the date the letter arrived
bank.explanation: The investigation clock runs from the oral notice. Because written confirmation came after 10 business days, the bank need not provisionally credit, but it must still investigate and resolve the error.

bank.question: Day 9 after a customer's dispute: the investigation needs another two weeks. What must the bank do to use the longer period?
options: Ask the customer to agree in writing to the longer investigation period
Report the open dispute to the CFPB and wait for its instructions
Close the account straight away to stop any further losses occurring on it
Provisionally credit by day 10 and tell the customer within two business days
bank.explanation: To use up to 45 days (or 90 where it applies), the bank must provisionally credit within 10 business days, tell the customer within two business days and give full use of the funds.

bank.question: A disputes analyst wants to hold back part of a provisional credit. Under what condition does Regulation E allow holding back up to USD 50?
options: When it reasonably believes an unauthorised transfer occurred and liability rules are met
Whenever the customer's account balance is low at the time of the dispute
When the merchant has formally disputed the customer's version of events
When the customer has already filed a complaint with the CFPB about it
bank.explanation: 1005.11(c)(2)(i) lets the bank withhold up to USD 50 if it has a reasonable basis to believe an unauthorised transfer occurred and has met 1005.6(a).

bank.question: A notice of error concerns a transfer made 20 days after the customer's first deposit into a new account. Which periods apply?
options: 10 business days and 45 days, as for any account
5 business days and 30 days, as new accounts are simpler
20 business days instead of 10, and 90 days instead of 45
No error resolution rights apply to accounts this new at all
bank.explanation: For transfers within 30 days after the first deposit, the 10-business-day period becomes 20, and the 45-day period becomes 90.

bank.question: A bank reverses a provisional credit after finding no error. Which additional step does Regulation E require?
options: Charge an overdraft fee on any item that the reversal causes to bounce
Freeze the account for 30 days in case the customer disputes again
Notify the debit and honour items for five business days without overdraft charges
Ask the customer to reimburse the bank's investigation costs in full
bank.explanation: 1005.11(d)(2) requires notice of the date and amount of the debit and that the bank will honour third-party items and preauthorised transfers for five business days without overdraft charges, as described.

bank.question: The CFPB found Bank of America acted abusively in its 2022 prepaid card case. Which conduct was described as abusive?
options: Reapplying the fraud filter to deny claims already investigated and paid
Paying unemployment benefits to recipients on prepaid debit cards
Answering cardholders' phone calls more slowly than in past years
Signing benefit delivery contracts with 12 different US state governments
bank.explanation: The CFPB described retroactively applying the fraud filter to deny previously paid notices of error as abusive. The original denials and freezes were unfair.

bank.question: A customer notices an unauthorised transfer on a statement sent 75 days ago and reports it today. More unauthorised transfers happened after day 60. Which is accurate?
options: She has no rights at all because more than 60 days have passed
She is liable for everything, including the transfers before day 60
The bank must refund everything regardless of when she reported it
She may owe later transfers the bank shows timely notice would have prevented
bank.explanation: Under 1005.6(b)(3), failure to report within 60 days of the statement can make the consumer liable for later transfers the bank shows would have been prevented. Extenuating circumstances can extend the time.

bank.question: A fraud team proposes freezing every account with a disputed card transaction until the investigation ends. What does the 2022 Wells Fargo order suggest?
options: Freezing every account is always required in fraud cases
Freezing accounts when lesser restraints are available can be unfair
Account freezes fall outside consumer protection law
Freezes are always fine if the deposit agreement allows them in writing
bank.explanation: The CFPB found Wells Fargo unfairly froze accounts in suspected fraud cases when lesser restraints were available. Controls should be proportionate.

bank.question: Grace hires a bank loan originator on 1 March 2026. He is registered in NMLSR. Before he originates a mortgage, which combination meets 1026.36(f)(3)?
options: NMLSR background check, credit report, NMLSR findings, fitness decision, training
NMLSR registration only, because registration replaces all of the bank's checks
A credit report only, because he is already an experienced loan originator
Periodic training only, because background checks are optional for bank employees
bank.explanation: The bank must get the background check, credit report and NMLSR information, decide the person meets the standards before they originate, and provide periodic training.

bank.question: A bank's screening shows a loan originator candidate was convicted 12 years ago of a felony involving fraud. No consent from a regulator applies. What does 1026.36(f)(3)(ii) mean for the hire?
options: He qualifies because more than seven years have passed since then
He qualifies if a senior manager vouches for his honesty
He does not meet the standard to act as a loan originator
He qualifies after completing one year of probation
bank.explanation: The seven-year look-back applies to felonies generally, but a felony involving fraud, dishonesty, breach of trust or money laundering disqualifies at any time, unless the relevant consent has been obtained.

bank.question: A bank wants to save time by giving the Loan Estimate at the first in-person meeting, five business days after it received the online application. What is the issue?
options: There is no issue at all if it is delivered in person
It is too early, so the bank must wait a few more days
The Loan Estimate is late; it was due by the third business day
The timing rule only applies to refinance loans, not to home purchases
bank.explanation: 1026.19(e)(1)(iii)(A) requires delivery or mailing no later than the third business day after the application is received.

bank.question: A mortgage borrower receives the Closing Disclosure by email the day before closing. Ignoring special exceptions, what is the issue?
options: The consumer must receive it at least three business days before consummation
There is no issue at all, as long as it arrives before the consumer signs anything
The Closing Disclosure is optional for banks that are supervised by the CFPB
It must always be posted by mail and can never be sent by email to anyone
bank.explanation: 1026.19(f)(1)(ii)(A) requires receipt no later than three business days before consummation, with defined exceptions such as timeshares.

bank.question: After 21 July 2026, a compliance analyst asks whether the bank still needs fair lending training for loan officers. What is the best answer?
options: No: removing the effects test ended the bank's fair lending duties
Only for staff working in states that have their own fair lending laws
Only if the CFPB, rather than the OCC, examines the bank in this exam cycle
Yes: intentional discrimination, discouragement and notice duties remain
bank.explanation: The 2026 amendment removed disparate impact from Regulation B. ECOA and Regulation B still ban discrimination on a prohibited basis, discouragement, and require proper adverse action notices.

bank.question: Which statement best describes how the amended Regulation B treats discouragement?
options: Any statement at all that leaves an applicant with a negative impression of the bank or its products
Statements the creditor knows or should know would make a reasonable person expect denial on a prohibited basis
Nothing, because the discouragement rule was removed from Regulation B entirely by the 2026 amendment
Only written advertising, so spoken statements made by loan officers in branches are no longer covered at all
bank.explanation: The amended 1002.4(b) covers oral or written statements, including images, that the creditor knows or should know would cause a reasonable person to believe they'd be denied or offered worse terms because of a prohibited basis.

bank.question: A bank denies an application and sends a notice saying only 'internal standards not met'. Under Regulation B, what is wrong?
options: It must state specific reasons, or disclose the right to get them
Nothing, because internal credit standards are confidential
It must also enclose the applicant's full credit file
It must be sent within five days of the decision
bank.explanation: An adverse action notice must contain a statement of specific reasons or disclose the applicant's right to a statement of specific reasons, along with other required content.

bank.question: A mortgage application lists the bank's name but not the individual loan originator's NMLSR ID. Which Regulation Z rule is engaged?
options: 1026.19(f), on the timing of the Closing Disclosure
1005.11, on the resolution of transfer errors
1026.36(g), on names and NMLSR IDs on loan documents
1016.5, on the annual privacy notice sent to customers
bank.explanation: 1026.36(g) requires the organisation's and the primary individual loan originator's names and NMLSR IDs on the application, the Loan Estimate and Closing Disclosure, the note and the security instrument.

bank.question: A customer files a complaint through the CFPB portal about a mortgage escrow error. The bank needs more than 15 days to investigate. What is the appropriate approach?
options: Ignore the portal and reply to the customer by letter after 90 days
Close the complaint in the portal marked as 'no response needed'
Say the response is in progress and give a final response within 60 days
Forward it to the escrow vendor and let the vendor answer it on its own terms
bank.explanation: The CFPB says companies generally respond in 15 days, and where needed indicate the response is in progress and provide a final response within 60 days.

bank.question: Complaints about a service provider's call centre are rising. The bank logs only complaints made directly to its branches. What does the CFPB manual expect?
options: All complaints, including about service providers, from every channel
Only complaints made in person at branches need to be recorded
Complaints about vendors belong only in the vendor's own complaint process
Only complaints that customers put in writing need to be logged
bank.explanation: Examiners assess whether complaints, regardless of channel and whether about the entity or its service providers, are recorded, categorised and resolved promptly.

bank.question: A bank's privacy notice says it does not share with nonaffiliated third parties for marketing. It now wants to start. Which is the correct sequence?
options: Share the data now and update the privacy notice at next year's annual mailing
Share only customers' email addresses, which are not covered by Regulation P
Share once the insurer signs a written promise not to sell the data to anyone else
Revised notice and opt-out, a reasonable wait, then share only non-opted-out data
bank.explanation: Sharing outside the exceptions requires notice, an opt-out notice and a reasonable opportunity to opt out first. Changing practice also ends any annual notice exception.

bank.question: Which statement about the scope of Regulation P notices is correct?
options: Every person who visits a branch must be handed an annual privacy notice
Customers get initial and generally annual notices; one-off consumers mainly before sharing
Only borrowers, not depositors, are entitled to receive privacy notices
Former customers must keep receiving annual privacy notices for life
bank.explanation: Regulation P distinguishes customers, who get notices when the relationship starts and generally yearly, from consumers, who get notice before disclosure to nonaffiliated third parties outside exceptions. Former customers do not need annual notices.

bank.question: A bank collects its own overdue loans in-house under its own name. Its staff use threatening language. Which statement is most accurate?
options: Regulation F may not apply, but the conduct can still be a UDAAP
No federal consumer law applies to a bank's own in-house collections
Only state criminal law can apply to threatening collection calls
It is lawful as long as the debt itself is valid and overdue
bank.explanation: A creditor collecting its own debts in its own name is generally outside Regulation F's debt collector definition, but UDAAP applies to any covered person, so abusive or deceptive collection is still unlawful.

bank.question: Which statement about recent CFPB consent order terminations (Citibank 2025, Regions 2025, Trustmark 2025) is the best compliance lesson?
options: Banks can now stop their fair lending and fee practice reviews
Terminated orders show the original conduct was always legal
Priorities can change, but the laws and CMS expectations still apply
Only state law now governs consumer protection for US banks of every size
bank.explanation: The CFPB pages show orders ended early after obligations were met or on motion. The laws (ECOA, CFPA, EFTA and others) remain, and banks still need a working CMS.

bank.question: An examiner reviews a bank's consumer complaint process and finds complaints are closed quickly but no one looks for patterns. Which CMS weakness is this?
options: Complaints are being resolved too slowly
Complaints are not used to find risks and drive corrective action
The bank offers too many complaint channels
The bank is paying too much customer redress
bank.explanation: The manual expects management to monitor complaints to identify risks of harm and CMS deficiencies, and take prospective and retrospective corrective action.

bank.question: On the eve of the exam, which package best shows a strong consumer CMS?
options: A marketing brochure, the annual report and the latest share price
A single compliance policy approved by the board five years ago
A list of all employees, their job titles, their managers and their salary bands
Board reports, policies, training records, monitoring, audit and complaint fixes
bank.explanation: Examiners assess oversight, policies, training, monitoring and audit, and complaint response. Evidence across all parts, including fixes, is what a strong CMS looks like.
